title: The end of the Amazon rubber monopoly, 1912
summary: The Amazon lost the rubber trade to plantations grown from its own seed. Henry Wickham had taken seeds out of Brazil in 1876; the British government planted them in Malaysia, Ceylon and tropical Africa, and by 1899 Ceylon alone had between fifteen hundred and sixteen hundred acres under rubber. Plantation latex could be produced with greater efficiency and productivity than latex tapped from wild trees scattered through forest, so it cost less, and with the lower price the British Empire took the world rubber market. The railway finished in 1912 arrived too late; the price fell and the first boom closed the same year. This is the shape of the thesis in one commodity: what Brazil sold was decided elsewhere, and so was when it stopped selling it.
